claims.text: Mergify states that with 20 PRs per day and a 30-minute CI pipeline, going from no batching to batches of 4 reduces CI time from 10 hours to 2.5 hours, a 75% reduction in CI resource usage.
Graphite reports that companies enabling Parallel CI on its merge queue saw 1.5x faster merges including CI time (33% decrease at p95, 26% at p75).
Graphite reports customers heavily using stacked PRs saw up to 2.5x faster merges with Parallel CI (60% decrease at p95, 34% decrease at p75).
Aviator states that increasing batch_size from 1 to 3 lets the queue merge 6 PRs instead of 2 in the same time it takes to run 2 CI cycles.

Mergify's example: with batch_size 3 and max_parallel_checks 2, given 7 queued PRs and a 10-minute CI pipeline, the first 6 PRs merge in 10 minutes instead of the hour required for sequential validation.
Mergify reports that its own merge queue, which tested every PR alone, choked on a morning when a burst of agent PRs landed faster than CI could clear them.
Mergify made batch_size accept a {min, max} object so the queue stays at min when parallel-check slots are plentiful and grows batches only when the queue backs up.

Before Mergify's dynamic batch-size change, 100% of its speculative checks were size 1; the first size-2 batch in its history fired on June 16 at 07:01 UTC, during a European morning with agent PRs stacking up.
Mergify states that its dynamic batch sizing did not raise throughput; the post says it will not claim a throughput increase.
Mergify runs parallel speculative checks and pays for the reliability and velocity in cost, specifically five bare-metal CI slots.
Mergify's RCV theorem states that a merge queue can optimize only two of reliability, cost and velocity at a time.
Under Mergify's RCV framing, parallel speculative checks give reliability plus velocity but waste CI runs when a PR ahead in the queue fails.
Under Mergify's RCV framing, sequential validation gives reliability plus low cost but caps throughput at one PR per CI run.
Under Mergify's RCV framing, batch mode gives velocity plus low cost, but hidden failures inside a passing batch can land on main.
Mergify advises lowering batch size and parallelism for repositories with frequent flaky or failing PRs to limit wasted work, and sizing for peak load rather than averages.
Mergify's Two-step CI runs fast preliminary tests when a PR is created or updated to gate queue entry, and exhaustive pre-merge tests just before merge, to keep queue-time CI short.

Graphite's Parallel CI only runs more CI when CI fails in the merge queue, so cost is low if tests are not flaky; a failure evicts the PR and restarts speculative runs for subsequent PRs, producing extra CI runs without slowing time-to-merge versus having it disabled.
In Graphite's parallel CI example with concurrency 3, when PR C fails, C is evicted, the speculative runs C←D and C←D←E are canceled, and CI restarts for D and D←E.

Graphite suggests choosing parallel CI concurrency to match peak PR volume given CI runtime: for 30-minute CI and 3 PRs per 30 minutes at peak, 3 concurrent runs give the most benefit; flaky repos should start lower.
Graphite's parallel CI can run CI on every PR in a stack individually (strongest correctness) or only on the topmost PR in the stack (fewer CI runs, relaxed per-PR guarantees).

Graphite's batching feature, in private beta, isolates a failing stack in a failed batch either by full parallel isolation (default, fast) or by bisection (fewer CI runs, as each iteration clears half the remaining stacks).
Trunk states that batching saves CI cost but, when a batch fails, bisection and retesting to isolate the failure can slow CI and raise total costs.
Trunk states that testing in parallel can be combined with batching and requires available CI workers and money for additional CI resources.
GitHub merge queue has a build concurrency setting of 1 to 100 that throttles concurrent merge_group CI builds, and merge limits of 1 to 100 PRs per merge.
In GitHub merge queue, jumping a PR to the top of the queue forces a full rebuild of all in-progress PRs, and heavy use can slow merge velocity.
